13.s: A gateway differs from a router chiefly because a gateway:
o: Operates only as a physical cable
Broadcasts every frame to all ports
13.x: A gateway joins networks that use different protocols and may operate across all or upper OSI layers.
13.tq: Discriminate between two nearby networking devices by their interoperability function.
13.sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

13.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with its transmission mode?
1. Radio or television broadcast — Simplex
2. Walkie-talkie — Half duplex
3. Telephone conversation — Full duplex
Select the correct answer.
13.x: Simplex permits one-way transmission, half duplex permits two-way transmission one at a time, and full duplex permits simultaneous two-way transmission.
13.tq: Compare the direction and simultaneity of communication.
13.sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

13.s: Which transmission mode is used when communication can occur in both directions, but not simultaneously?
13.x: Half duplex permits communication in both directions, but one direction operates at a time, as in a walkie-talkie.
13.tq: Focus on the phrase 'both ways, one at a time'.
13.sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

13.s:
Consider the following statements about Internet connection media:
1. DSL uses telephone copper lines.
2. Cable Internet uses coaxial television cable.
3. Fibre Internet transmits data as light pulses through optical fibre.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
13.x: DSL uses telephone copper lines, cable Internet uses coaxial TV cable, and fibre Internet uses optical fibre carrying light pulses.
13.tq: Match each technology with its physical transmission medium.
13.sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

13.s: Satellite Internet generally consists of which three segments?
13.x: Satellite Internet has space, ground and user (VSAT) segments and does not require a terrestrial wire connection.
13.tq: Recall the three-part system architecture.
13.sec: Network devices and transmission - router, switch, hub, modem, duplex, DSL/cable/fibre  [other exams]

13.s: Which of the following represents the correct top-to-bottom order of the OSI model?
o: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
Application, Session, Presentation, Network, Transport, Data Link, Physical
Presentation, Application, Session, Transport, Data Link, Network, Physical
13.x: From the top layer downward, the OSI model is Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link and Physical.
13.tq: Use the first and last layers, then verify the middle sequence.
13.sec: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices  [other exams]

13.s:
Match the following OSI layers with their associated functions or protocols:
List-I (Layer)
a. Presentation
b. Session
c. Transport
d. Data Link

List-II (Function or protocol)
i. TCP and UDP
ii. Encryption, compression and formats
 iii. Opens and closes sessions
 iv. MAC addressing and frame forwarding

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
13.x: The Presentation layer handles encryption, compression and formats; the Session layer opens and closes sessions; the Transport layer uses TCP and UDP; and the Data Link layer handles MAC-based frame operations.
13.tq: Start with the distinctive TCP/UDP and MAC pairs.
13.sec: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices  [other exams]

13.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched with the OSI layer?
1. HTTP — Application layer
2. IP — Network layer
3. MAC — Data Link layer
4. Cables — Physical layer
Select the correct answer.
13.x: HTTP is an Application-layer protocol, IP belongs to the Network layer, MAC is associated with the Data Link layer, and cables operate at the Physical layer.
13.tq: Use protocol and device layer matching to validate each statement.
13.sec: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices  [other exams]

13.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
13.x: A modem is associated with the Physical layer because it modulates and demodulates signals; it is not a Transport-layer device.
13.tq: Find the device placed at the wrong OSI layer.
13.sec: OSI model - seven layers → protocols/devices  [other exams]

13.s: An organisation notices that a particular website is inaccessible to users of one Internet service provider, while users of another provider can access it. Which explanation is consistent with this situation?
o: The provider may be using DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering
The OSI model has ceased to operate for that website
All websites have been permanently removed from the Internet
A PAN has automatically become a WAN
13.x: ISPs may block sites through DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering on HTTPS. Consequently, blocklists and access results can differ between ISPs.
13.tq: Apply the technical mechanism to the observed provider-specific outcome.
13.sec: Universal angles

13.s: Which of the following correctly states the change in Internet connections in India mentioned for the period 2014–2024?
13.x: Internet connections increased from 25.15 crore in 2014 to 96.96 crore in 2024.
13.tq: Check both the direction of change and the units.
13.sec: Universal angles

13.s: BharatNet fibre, as indicated for 2025–26, reaches approximately how many gram panchayats?
13.x: BharatNet fibre reaches approximately 2.18 lakh gram panchayats according to the stated 2025–26 figure.
13.tq: Distinguish the lakh figure from crore and reversed-number distractors.
13.sec: Universal angles

13.s: Which set of issues was discussed by Chief Minister Naidu and Sunil Mittal in relation to Andhra Pradesh?
o: Only the replacement of optical fibre by copper cable
Coal mining, irrigation dams and inland waterways
Last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station
Only satellite launching and missile testing
13.x: The discussion concerned last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station for Andhra Pradesh.
13.tq: Identify the complete issue cluster rather than a partial distractor.
13.sec: Universal angles

14.s: Who founded LinkedIn, which is primarily used for professional networking?
14.x: LinkedIn was founded by Reid Hoffman in 2003 and is used mainly for professional networking.

o: LinkedIn has been owned by Microsoft since 2016.

14.x: Twitter was renamed X in 2023 following Elon Musk's takeover.
14.tq: Distinguish the renaming year from the platform's founding and ownership years.

14.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Viral — Content spreading rapidly by sharing
Influencer — Content that spreads rapidly through sharing
Wall — Profile space where posts appear on Facebook
14.x: An influencer is a user whose following can sway opinions and buying decisions. Content spreading rapidly through sharing is described as viral.
14.tq: Find the swapped meanings among closely related social-media terms.
14.sec: Social media - platforms → founder/parent, content terms

14.s: The term ‘Folksonomy’ in social media refers to:
o: Paid promotion by a platform owner
14.x: Folksonomy means user-created tagging or classification, also called social tagging.
14.tq: Test the exact meaning of a technical content-classification term.
14.sec: Social media - platforms → founder/parent, content terms

14.s: Social Media Optimisation (SMO) primarily aims at:
14.x: SMO stands for Social Media Optimisation and involves raising reach through social platforms.
14.tq: Identify the practical purpose of the named digital-media activity.
14.sec: Social media - platforms → founder/parent, content terms

14.s: Hashtag (#) was popularised on which social-media platform?
14.x: The hashtag was popularised on Twitter.
14.tq: Associate the content term with the platform that popularised it, not merely a platform where it is used.
14.sec: Social media - platforms → founder/parent, content terms

14.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Twitter is renamed X
B. LinkedIn comes under Microsoft ownership
C. LinkedIn is founded
D. Facebook is founded
14.x: LinkedIn was founded in 2003, Facebook in 2004, LinkedIn came under Microsoft ownership in 2016, and Twitter was renamed X in 2023.
14.tq: Place the dated platform events using the first and last events as anchors.
14.sec: Social media - platforms → founder/parent, content terms

14.s:
Consider the following statements about Mobile Number Portability (MNP):
1. A Haryana pilot preceded wider implementation.
2. MNP began within a circle on 20 January 2011.
3. Full nationwide MNP started on 3 July 2015.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
14.x: All three statements are correct. The Haryana pilot was held on 25 November 2010, followed by within-circle implementation in January 2011 and nationwide MNP in July 2015.
14.tq: Verify the sequence of pilot, within-circle implementation and nationwide expansion.
14.sec: Mobile telephony - first handheld call, SIM, MNP, Android, QR, NFC, market rank

14.s: The Haryana pilot associated with Mobile Number Portability was conducted on:
14.x: The Haryana pilot for Mobile Number Portability was conducted on 25 November 2010.
14.tq: Separate the pilot date from the later implementation dates.

14.s: What does the abbreviation SIM stand for in mobile telephony?
14.x: SIM stands for Subscriber Identity Module.

14.sec: Mobile telephony - first handheld call, SIM, MNP, Android, QR, NFC, market rank

14.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Android?
o: A mobile operating system developed by Google and built on the Linux kernel
A payment protocol operating only through Bluetooth
A mobile network standard developed by Denso Wave
A mobile-number portability mechanism operated by RBI

14.s:
With reference to QR codes, consider the following statements:
1. QR stands for Quick Response.
2. QR codes were designed by Denso Wave in Japan.
3. Their original design in 1994 was for the car industry.
4. They are read quickly by a phone camera.

14.s: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of Near Field Communication (NFC) as described in mobile technology?
o: It supports data rates of about 106–424 kbps.
It generally works over a distance of a few centimetres.
It permits easier pairing and uses less power than Bluetooth.
It normally requires a greater operating range than Bluetooth.
14.x: NFC works over a few centimetres, supports approximately 106–424 kbps, and generally offers easier pairing and lower power use than Bluetooth. It does not require a greater operating range than Bluetooth.
14.tq: Reject the reversed comparison in the NFC–Bluetooth distinction.

WiMAX replaced LTE as the dominant 4G technology.

Their possible effect on document writers’ livelihoods and the assurance that SROs are not being privatised
Their exclusive operation by the Singapore delegation
Their restriction to only 50 government services

28.s: Which one of the following is NOT recommended as an online safety practice?
o: Being cautious while sharing personal or sensitive information
Accepting friend requests from unknown persons without caution
28.x: Accepting friend requests from unknown persons without caution is not a safe online practice. Strong passwords, verification before sharing and caution with sensitive information are recommended.
28.tq: Find the one unsafe practice among otherwise safe digital habits.

28.s: Which of the following is a set of recognised authentication methods?
o: Friend requests, QR codes and Wi-Fi names
Digital footprint, privacy settings and netiquette
28.x: Passwords, biometrics and multi-factor authentication are authentication methods used to verify a user's identity.
28.tq: Identify the option containing only methods belonging to the same functional category.
28.sec: Online safety practices - passwords, friend requests, privacy settings, 2FA, verify before sharing

28.s: A person receives a message from a friend urgently asking for money. Which is the safest immediate course of action?
o: Verify the request through another channel before making any payment
Transfer the money immediately because the request came from a known contact
Scan a QR code sent by the friend to receive the money
Click the accompanying link to confirm the friend's identity
28.x: A friend's account or identity may have been hacked, so the request should be independently verified before payment. Links or QR codes should not be clicked or scanned to receive money.
28.tq: Apply the cyber-hygiene rule to a realistic digital-fraud situation.
28.sec: Online safety practices - passwords, friend requests, privacy settings, 2FA, verify before sharing

28.s: Which of the following practices is specifically recommended for securing a wireless network?
o: Scanning every QR code received through messaging applications
Accepting unknown contacts to increase network access
28.x: Using WPA3 Wi-Fi is recommended as a cyber-hygiene measure. Keeping one's digital footprint low is also advised, whereas indiscriminate QR-code scanning and accepting unknown contacts are unsafe.
28.tq: Select the precise technical safety measure from closely related online behaviours.
28.sec: Online safety practices - passwords, friend requests, privacy settings, 2FA, verify before sharing

28.s: Nomophobia refers to:
o: Irrational fear of being without one's mobile phone
Fear of receiving unsolicited friend requests
Fear of sharing personal information online
28.x: Nomophobia is the irrational fear of being without one's mobile phone, including situations involving no signal, low battery or insufficient balance.
28.tq: Discriminate between a technical term and nearby digital-safety concepts.
28.sec: Online safety practices - passwords, friend requests, privacy settings, 2FA, verify before sharing

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021:

2. They provide for a grievance officer and a nodal contact.
3. Significant social media intermediaries are required to appoint a Resident Compliance Officer and submit monthly compliance reports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All three statements are correct. The 2021 Rules were notified under Section 87 of the IT Act, 2000 and prescribe grievance, nodal and additional compliance obligations for significant social media intermediaries.
28.tq: Check each statement against the legal framework before selecting the complete combination.
28.sec: Fact-check mechanisms - PIB FCU, tip lines, IT Rules amendments, Sahyog portal, court challenges

28.s: Under the April 2023 amendment to the IT Rules, an intermediary could lose safe-harbour protection when:
o: A platform received fewer than 100 complaints in a month
A court refused to hear a cybercrime petition
The PIB Fact Check Unit flagged content as fake concerning the business of the Central Government
Any private user described content as unpopular
28.x: The April 2023 amendment provided for loss of safe harbour where content concerning the business of the Central Government was flagged as fake by the PIB Fact Check Unit.
28.tq: Identify the authority and subject-matter combination attached to a legal consequence.
28.sec: Fact-check mechanisms - PIB FCU, tip lines, IT Rules amendments, Sahyog portal, court challenges

28.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. IT Rules, 2021 were notified
B. The PIB Fact Check Unit was set up
C. The FCU was formally notified under PIB
D. The April 2023 amendment to the IT Rules was issued
28.x: The PIB Fact Check Unit was set up in November 2019, the IT Rules were notified in 2021, the amendment followed in April 2023, and the FCU was formally notified in March 2024.
28.tq: Use the first and last dates, then place the intervening developments.
28.sec: Fact-check mechanisms - PIB FCU, tip lines, IT Rules amendments, Sahyog portal, court challenges

28.s: The PIB Fact Check Unit was formally notified in:
28.x: The PIB Fact Check Unit was formally notified in March 2024. This was distinct from its earlier establishment in November 2019.

28.sec: Fact-check mechanisms - PIB FCU, tip lines, IT Rules amendments, Sahyog portal, court challenges

28.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the judicial developments concerning the PIB Fact Check Unit notification and amendment?
o: The Supreme Court stayed the March 2024 notification, and the Bombay High Court struck down the 2023 amendment in September 2024.
The Bombay High Court stayed the March 2024 notification, and the Supreme Court struck down the 2023 amendment in September 2024.
The Supreme Court struck down the March 2024 notification before it was issued.
Both the notification and amendment were upheld by the Bombay High Court.
28.x: The Supreme Court stayed the FCU notification in March 2024, while the Bombay High Court struck down the 2023 FCU amendment in September 2024.

28.s: SAHYOG Portal is operated by which organisation and for what principal purpose?
o: I4C under the Ministry of Home Affairs, for takedown notices
PIB under the Ministry of Education, for issuing school certificates
NSS under the Ministry of Statistics, for collecting literacy data
AIGDF under the Ministry of Electronics and IT, for gaming licences
28.x: SAHYOG Portal is run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs for takedown notices, alongside the Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.

It aims to provide one digitally literate person in every rural family and was launched by the Prime Minister at Gandhinagar.
It is a financial-literacy programme for adults aged 15 years and above under ULLAS.
28.x: PMGDISHA promotes digital literacy among rural people, with the aim of having one digitally literate person in every family; it was launched by the Prime Minister at Gandhinagar.

3. Its ‘Critical Life Skills’ component includes digital literacy and financial literacy.
4. Himachal Pradesh became the fifth State or Union Territory to achieve full functional literacy.

28.s: The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 treats which combination as important educational emphases and a counter-measure against fake news?

Only vocational licensing and biometric enrolment
28.x: NEP 2020 stresses critical thinking and civic engagement. Critical-thinking education in curricula can help counter fake news.
28.tq: Select the constructive educational pair rather than digital behaviours that amplify misinformation.
28.sec: Digital literacy - levels, Computer Literacy Day, NSS data, school curriculum

28.s: Which statement best reflects the gender gap in India's internet use?
o: Women constitute nearly all of India's internet users
Women constitute about one-third of India's internet users
Women constitute less than one-tenth of India's internet users
Men and women have exactly equal shares of internet users

28.tq: Identify the approximate share without reversing the gender comparison.

28.s: Doxxing is best described as:
o: Using websites to express one's own grievances
Repeatedly contacting a person online against their will
Sending a verified government notification to a platform
Publicly sharing a person's private information online without consent to harm or shame them
28.x: Doxxing involves publicly sharing private information such as a real name, location or workplace online without consent, generally to harm or shame the person.
28.tq: Distinguish disclosure of private information from monitoring, venting and trolling.
28.sec: Online behaviour terms - cyber venting, trolling, cyberbullying, doxxing, cyberstalking, remedies

28.s: Which statement regarding doxxing is correct?
o: It has no universal legal definition and may be prosecuted under stalking, harassment or cyber-crime laws
It has a universal, self-contained legal definition in all jurisdictions
It is prosecuted only under a separate offence named doxxing
It is legally identical to cyber venting in every case
28.x: Doxxing has no universal legal definition. Depending on the conduct, prosecution may rely on stalking, harassment or cyber-crime laws.
28.tq: Watch for the absolute legal-definition trap and choose the qualified statement.
28.sec: Online behaviour terms - cyber venting, trolling, cyberbullying, doxxing, cyberstalking, remedies

28.s: Cyberstalking refers to:
o: Posting deliberately provocative material to derail a discussion
Teaching adults to use digital payment systems
Repeatedly monitoring or contacting a person online against that person's will
Sharing one's own grievances through websites
28.x: Cyberstalking is the repeated monitoring or contacting of a person online against the person's will.
28.tq: Separate persistent unwanted monitoring from trolling and cyberbullying.
28.sec: Online behaviour terms - cyber venting, trolling, cyberbullying, doxxing, cyberstalking, remedies

28.s: Which of the following pairs of legal provisions and remedies is correctly matched?
o: IT Act Section 66E—privacy violation; IT Act Section 67—obscene material; BNS Section 78—stalking including monitoring electronic communication
IT Act Section 66E—financial literacy; IT Act Section 67—digital empowerment; BNS Section 78—takedown notices only
IT Act Section 66E—election tip line; IT Act Section 67—Wi-Fi security; BNS Section 78—doxxing definition
IT Act Section 66E—civic engagement; IT Act Section 67—universal literacy; BNS Section 78—password recovery
28.x: Section 66E of the IT Act concerns privacy violation, Section 67 concerns obscene material, and Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita covers stalking, including monitoring electronic communication.

28.tq: Match the initiative with its partner organisation and subject area.

28.s: Which one of the following is an appropriate email netiquette practice?
o: Forwarding chain mails to all contacts
Typing the entire message in capital letters
Using a clear subject line and a polite greeting
Sending the message without checking the recipients
28.x: A clear subject line, polite greeting and verification of recipients are appropriate email practices. Typing in all capitals may be perceived as shouting, while chain-mail forwarding should be avoided.
28.tq: Identify the positive ‘Do’ practice and reject the email-specific ‘Don’t’ practices.
28.sec: Netiquettes - rules for email, social media, online meetings, forums (dos and don'ts)

28.s: In the context of social-media netiquette, which of the following is NOT appropriate?
o: Posting another person's photograph without consent
Respecting the privacy of other users
Giving credit to the original source
28.x: Posting another person's photograph or data without consent violates social-media netiquette. Verification, privacy protection and source credit are appropriate practices.
28.tq: Find the single privacy-violating action among otherwise constructive social-media practices.
28.sec: Netiquettes - rules for email, social media, online meetings, forums (dos and don'ts)

28.s:
Consider the following statements regarding online meetings:
1. Participants should join on time.
2. A participant should remain unmuted even when not speaking.
3. Recording a meeting without permission is improper.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Joining on time and avoiding recording without permission are proper practices. Participants should mute themselves when they are not speaking; therefore, statement 2 is false.
28.tq: Split the options by checking the meeting-specific mute and permission rules.
28.sec: Netiquettes - rules for email, social media, online meetings, forums (dos and don'ts)

28.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with forum etiquette?
o: Reading rules and FAQs — appropriate practice
28.x: Reading the rules and FAQs is appropriate forum behaviour. Spamming, flaming and repeatedly cross-posting are improper practices.
28.tq: Match the constructive forum behaviour with the correct medium-specific rule.
28.sec: Netiquettes - rules for email, social media, online meetings, forums (dos and don'ts)

28.s: The principle that digital freedom should be accompanied by digital responsibility primarily implies which of the following?
o: Online dialogue should be constructive and privacy should be respected
Only government agencies should participate in online discussions
Digital platforms should prohibit all disagreement
Users may communicate without considering consequences
28.x: Digital freedom is linked with responsible conduct, including constructive online dialogue and respect for privacy. It does not imply unrestricted irresponsible behaviour or a ban on disagreement.
28.tq: Apply the underlying principle to distinguish responsible participation from absolute or restrictive claims.
28.sec: Netiquettes - rules for email, social media, online meetings, forums (dos and don'ts)

28.s: Which of the following is a characteristic of a responsible digital citizen?
o: Disclosing personal data to establish trust
28.x: A responsible digital citizen identifies misinformation, verifies sources, protects personal data, respects privacy and participates in civil discourse.
28.tq: Choose the behaviour that combines verification with responsible digital participation.
28.sec: Digital citizenship - rights, responsibilities, digital footprint

28.s:
Consider the following statements about digital citizenship:
1. Protecting personal data is a responsibility of a digital citizen.
2. Respecting privacy is part of responsible online conduct.
3. Civil discourse is inconsistent with digital citizenship.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: Protecting personal data and respecting privacy are responsibilities of digital citizens. Civil discourse is an important component of digital citizenship, so statement 3 is false.
28.tq: Locate the negatively worded statement that reverses a core responsibility.
28.sec: Digital citizenship - rights, responsibilities, digital footprint

28.s: Which of the following is included among the rights-related aspects of digital citizenship?
o: Unrestricted publication of another person's data
28.x: Online grievance redressal, e-consultations and access to open government data are rights-related aspects of digital citizenship. The other alternatives conflict with privacy or digital participation.
28.tq: Select the recognised digital-governance facility rather than an exaggerated restriction or privacy violation.
28.sec: Digital citizenship - rights, responsibilities, digital footprint

28.s: The AP Grama and Ward Sachivalayam system is cited in the context of which aspect of digital citizenship?
o: Online grievance redressal and digital governance
28.x: AP Grama and Ward Sachivalayam is an example associated with digital-governance rights and services, including online grievance redressal and citizen consultations.
28.tq: Use the place-based example to identify the relevant digital-governance function.
28.sec: Digital citizenship - rights, responsibilities, digital footprint

28.s: What is meant by a digital footprint?
o: The physical location of a computer network
A government identity document used offline
A software programme that blocks advertisements
The trail of data a person leaves online
28.x: A digital footprint is the trail of data that a person leaves through online activities. Keeping it low can reduce exposure to fraud.
28.tq: Distinguish the exact definition from physical, administrative and software-related distractors.
28.sec: Digital citizenship - rights, responsibilities, digital footprint

28.s: Keeping one's digital footprint low is significant because it can reduce exposure to which of the following?
28.x: Reducing the amount of personal data left online can reduce exposure to fraud. It does not mean avoiding legitimate digital-government services.
28.tq: Link the preventive digital practice with its stated risk-reduction outcome.
28.sec: Digital citizenship - rights, responsibilities, digital footprint

28.s: A false message is circulated because the sender believes it to be true and has no intention to deceive. This is best described as:
28.x: Misinformation is false content spread without an intent to deceive, including innocent mistakes and rumours. Deliberate creation of false content is disinformation.
28.tq: Separate the three similar terms by testing the sender’s intention and the truth of the content.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s: False content deliberately created to achieve political, social or economic goals is known as:
28.x: Disinformation is false content deliberately created to achieve political, social or economic objectives. Misinformation lacks an intent to deceive, while malinformation is genuine information used harmfully.
28.tq: Focus on the intention behind creating false content to distinguish the confusable terms.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s: Genuine information shared with the intention of causing harm, such as leaked private data, is termed:
28.x: Malinformation consists of genuine information shared to cause harm; leaked private data is an example. It differs from false information in misinformation and disinformation.
28.tq: Use the truth-versus-falsity distinction before considering the harmful intention.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Misinformation is false content spread without an intent to deceive.
2. Disinformation is deliberately created false content.
3. Malinformation consists of genuine information shared to cause harm.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: All three statements correctly distinguish the terms: misinformation lacks deceptive intent, disinformation is deliberately false, and malinformation uses genuine information harmfully.
28.tq: Check each term against the two decisive criteria: truth value and intention.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s: Which of the following is identified as a cause of fake news?
o: Profit motive through clicks and advertising revenue
28.x: Profit motive, including the pursuit of clicks and advertising revenue, is a cause of fake news. Fake news may also produce polarisation and misinformation cascades.
28.tq: Identify the economic incentive directly associated with the spread of fake news.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s:
Fake news can contribute to which of the following effects?
1. Polarisation
2. Misinformation cascades
3. Automatic protection of privacy
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
28.x: Fake news can cause polarisation and misinformation cascades. It does not automatically protect privacy, so statement 3 is false.
28.tq: Reject the unrelated positive-sounding claim and retain the two stated consequences.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s: Filter bubbles and echo chambers are associated with algorithms that:
o: Prevent users from receiving any personalised content
Prioritise content according to user preferences and isolate users from other viewpoints
Remove every item of disputed information
28.x: Algorithms can prioritise content matching a user’s preferences and thereby isolate the user from other viewpoints, producing filter bubbles or echo chambers.
28.tq: Match the mechanism of algorithmic personalisation with its social effect.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s: Which of the following is a measure mentioned for responding to deepfakes?
o: Removal of all online political content
A ban on every form of digital communication
ECI advisory requiring labels on AI-generated content in campaigns
28.x: Measures for responding to deepfakes include the ECI advisory on mandatory labels for AI content in campaigns, DPDP Act penalties and I4C takedowns.
28.tq: Identify the specific institutional response rather than an extreme blanket restriction.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s: Which institution or legal measure is correctly associated with the specified deepfake response?
o: EU AI Act — removal of grievance processes
ECI — prohibition of all campaign communication
28.x: I4C is associated with takedowns. The DPDP Act is associated with penalties, while the EU AI Act mandates watermarking; the other pairings misstate the measures.
28.tq: Start from the sure institutional pair and eliminate reversed or exaggerated functions.
28.sec: Misinformation vs disinformation vs malinformation - terms, deepfakes, echo chambers

28.s: Which of the following is a counter-measure against election misinformation while also respecting democratic freedoms?
o: Allowing platforms to spread verified and unverified content equally
Removing every controversial opinion without review
Media-literacy programmes and fact-checking, combined with proportionate platform policies
28.x: Media literacy, fact-checkers and platform policies to remove or down-rank fake content are counter-measures. Regulation is expected to avoid unnecessarily curbing free speech.
28.tq: Choose the balanced policy option that addresses misinformation without an absolute speech restriction.

Under the Information Technology Rules, 2021, platform duties include:
1. Due diligence.
2. Prompt removal of harmful content.
3. Grievance processes, particularly for content harmful to children.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
28.x: The stated platform duties under the IT Rules, 2021 include due diligence, prompt removal of harmful content and grievance processes, especially for content harmful to children.
28.tq: Test the complete set of duties and use the comprehensive option when all three are supported.
28.sec: Media literacy initiatives - election misinformation measures, platform self-regulation

28.s: Which of the following statements about minors and misinformation is correct?
o: Age-related restrictions are irrelevant to digital policy
Minors universally possess advanced skills to identify misinformation
Minors are excluded from all social-media regulation debates
Minors may lack the skills to distinguish truth from misinformation
28.x: Minors may lack the skills needed to distinguish truth from misinformation. This concern has contributed to debates over age-based social-media restrictions.
28.tq: Avoid the absolute claims and select the cautious statement about minors’ media-literacy skills.
28.sec: Media literacy initiatives - election misinformation measures, platform self-regulation

28.s: Which one of the following correctly states the sequence of countries mentioned in connection with social-media restrictions for persons below 16 years, beginning with Australia?
28.x: The countries mentioned are Australia, Indonesia, Malaysia, France and Canada. A similar proposal was stated to have been debated for India.
28.tq: Preserve the stated sequence and eliminate options that swap neighbouring countries.
28.sec: Media literacy initiatives - election misinformation measures, platform self-regulation

28.s: Which of the following developments is associated with the current debate on digital regulation?
o: The Supreme Court declaring that free speech has no online application
The Supreme Court weighing the IT Rules against free speech
The abolition of all IT Rules
The prohibition of all platform grievance mechanisms
28.x: The Supreme Court was stated to be weighing the relationship between the IT Rules and free speech. The other alternatives make unsupported absolute claims.
28.tq: Identify the precise constitutional-policy tension rather than an absolute judicial outcome.
28.sec: Universal angles

28.s: Doxxing of women protesters at Jantar Mantar is primarily relevant to which digital-society concern?
o: Open government data as a public right
Unauthorised exposure of personal information and online safety
28.x: Doxxing involves the unauthorised exposure of personal information and raises concerns relating to privacy and online safety. It is distinct from open government data and AI-content labelling.
28.tq: Connect the incident to the privacy and safety issue directly implicated by doxxing.
28.sec: Universal angles

28.s:
Assertion (A): Regulation of fake news must consider the protection of free speech.
Reason (R): Measures to curb misinformation may raise concerns about executive overreach when the government determines truth about itself.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
28.x: Both statements are true, and the risk of executive overreach explains why regulation intended to curb fake news must also protect free speech.
28.tq: Check whether the institutional-risk reason directly explains the need for a free-speech safeguard.
28.sec: Universal angles

28.s: The digital economy accounted for what percentage of national income in FY23, and what percentage was it projected to reach in FY25?
28.x: The digital economy accounted for 11.74% of national income in FY23 and was projected to reach 13.42% in FY25.
28.tq: Keep the actual and projected figures in their chronological order.
28.sec: Universal angles

28.s:
Arrange the following figures for internet connections in chronological order:
A. 96.96 crore in 2024
B. 25.15 crore in 2014
C. 13.42% projected digital-economy share in FY25
D. 11.74% digital-economy share in FY23
28.x: In chronological order, the figures refer to 25.15 crore connections in 2014, 11.74% in FY23, the projected 13.42% in FY25 and 96.96 crore connections in 2024. The ordering combines the dated figures as presented.
28.tq: Arrange the dated values first and use the year sequence to eliminate reversed orders.
28.sec: Universal angles

28.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: WHO — platform takedown authority under I4C
EU AI Act — online grievance redressal in Andhra Pradesh
ECI — classification of Gaming Disorder in ICD-11
28.x: AP Grama/Ward Sachivalayam is identified as a digital-governance model. I4C, the EU AI Act, ECI and WHO have different roles from those stated in the other pairs.
28.tq: Use institutional-role matching and reject swapped authorities.
28.sec: Universal angles

29.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the mode of operation of a computer virus?
o: It automatically spreads across networks without any user interaction
It attaches itself to files or programmes and generally requires the user to execute the infected file
It disguises itself as legitimate software and never modifies files
It records every keystroke without attaching to any file
29.x: A virus attaches to files or programmes and usually requires the user to execute the infected file. It may corrupt or delete data.
29.tq: Distinguish malware by its precise mechanism rather than by its general harmful effect.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s:
Consider the following statements about computer worms:
1. They can self-replicate across networks.
2. They require the user to execute an infected file before spreading.
3. They may consume network bandwidth.
4. They are regarded as the fastest-spreading type of malware.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 describes a typical virus; a worm spreads automatically without user interaction.
29.tq: Separate the closely related virus and worm mechanisms by checking the user-interaction condition.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s: A malicious programme is disguised as legitimate software, does not self-replicate and opens a backdoor into a system. It is best classified as a:
29.x: A Trojan is disguised as legitimate software, does not self-replicate and may open a backdoor for unauthorised access.
29.tq: Apply the three-part distinction of disguise, self-replication and backdoor access.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s: The AIIMS Delhi cyber incident of 2022 is associated with which type of malware?
29.x: The AIIMS Delhi attack of 2022 is cited as an example of ransomware, which encrypts files or systems and demands payment for restoration.
29.tq: Use the named incident as the anchor for identifying the malware category.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s: Which one of the following best describes spyware?
o: Software that secretly monitors users and steals passwords or banking data
A network of remotely controlled infected devices
Software that encrypts the master boot record and demands cryptocurrency
29.x: Spyware performs secret surveillance and may steal passwords and banking information from the user.
29.tq: Discriminate malware by its primary objective instead of its method of entry.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s: Adware is most commonly associated with which of the following?
o: Recording every keystroke entered by a user
Unwanted advertisements bundled with free or pirated software
29.x: Adware displays unwanted advertisements and is often bundled with free or pirated software.
29.tq: Match the malware name with its characteristic visible behaviour.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s: Which of the following is the principal feature of a rootkit?
o: It spreads only through infected removable files
It sends repeated advertising messages to users
It demands ransom in cryptocurrency after encrypting files
It obtains administrator-level access and hides other malware
29.x: A rootkit gains deep administrator-level access and conceals other malicious components, making it particularly difficult to detect.
29.tq: Identify the defining privilege and concealment feature of the malware.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s: A programme that records passwords, PINs, OTPs and card numbers by capturing every keystroke is known as a:
29.x: A keylogger records every keystroke, including passwords, PINs, OTPs and card numbers.
29.tq: Use the direct functional clue—recording keystrokes—to identify the malware.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s: A botnet is best described as:
o: A legitimate software package containing advertisements
A network of infected devices remotely controlled for activities such as DDoS attacks
A collection of encrypted files held for ransom
A virus that can operate only after a user opens an attachment
29.x: A botnet consists of infected ‘zombie’ devices controlled remotely and may be used for DDoS attacks, spam or crypto-mining.
29.tq: Identify the network-level concept from the words ‘infected devices’ and ‘remote control’.
29.sec: Malware types → mechanism (virus, worm, trojan, ransomware, spyware, adware, rootkit, keylogger, botnet)

29.s: The Creeper programme, associated with the year 1971, was developed in connection with which network?
29.x: Creeper appeared on ARPANET in 1971 and is recognised as the first self-replicating programme or virus. It was associated with Bob Thomas of BBN.
29.tq: Link the historical malware name with its year and network of origin.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with Elk Cloner?
o: A ransomware worm that used the EternalBlue exploit in 2017
The first virus in the wild, affecting Apple II computers in 1982
The first IBM-PC boot-sector virus, created in Lahore in 1986
A worm that sabotaged uranium centrifuges in Iran
29.x: Elk Cloner, created by Rich Skrenta, is regarded as the first virus in the wild and affected Apple II computers in 1982.
29.tq: Use the platform and historical status together to distinguish early named viruses.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s:
With reference to the Brain virus, consider the following statements:
1. It was an IBM-PC boot-sector virus.
2. It was associated with MS-DOS.
3. It originated in Lahore, Pakistan.
4. It was created in 1971 on ARPANET.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: Brain was the first IBM-PC MS-DOS boot-sector virus and was created by the Alvi brothers in Lahore, Pakistan, in 1986. Statement 4 refers to Creeper.
29.tq: Use platform, operating system and place to separate Brain from other early viruses.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: WannaCry is best described as:
o: A ransomware worm that spread by exploiting EternalBlue
A spyware programme developed by NSO Group
A botnet that hijacked Internet of Things devices
An Android vulnerability discovered by Promon
29.x: WannaCry was a ransomware worm that spread through the EternalBlue exploit in 2017. It has also been attributed to the Lazarus group of North Korea.
29.tq: Combine the malware type with the named exploit to identify the correct attack.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: Which of the following statements regarding Petya is correct?
o: It is a botnet made up of hijacked IoT devices.
It is a spyware programme requiring no user interaction.
It is an adware programme bundled with pirated software.
It is a ransomware that encrypts disk boot records.
29.x: Petya is ransomware that encrypts the master boot record or disk boot records. NotPetya, its later variant, notably affected Ukraine in 2017.
29.tq: Distinguish a named ransomware by the specific system component it encrypts.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: EternalBlue refers to which of the following?
o: An exploit of a Windows SMB vulnerability
A surveillance tool developed by NSO Group
An Android vulnerability found by Promon
29.x: EternalBlue exploited a flaw in Windows SMB. It was developed by the United States NSA and leaked by the Shadow Brokers in 2017.
29.tq: Distinguish an exploit from the malware that used it and from the organisation associated with spyware.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: Stuxnet was notable primarily because it:
o: Hijacked IoT devices to conduct DDoS attacks
Encrypted files on the computers of AIIMS Delhi
Targeted Iran’s Natanz uranium centrifuges using a worm with rootkit components
Affected Apple II computers as the first virus in the wild
29.x: Stuxnet was a worm containing rootkit components that sabotaged Siemens PLC-controlled uranium centrifuges at Iran’s Natanz facility.
29.tq: Connect the named malware with its distinctive target and industrial-control context.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Pegasus?
o: An Android vulnerability discovered by a Norwegian firm
A boot-sector virus created in Lahore
A ransomware worm developed by the United States NSA
A zero-click spyware associated with NSO Group of Israel
29.x: Pegasus is state-grade zero-click spyware associated with Israel’s NSO Group and can exploit zero-days without requiring user interaction.
29.tq: Separate spyware identity, developer and zero-click capability from other named threats.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: StrandHogg is associated with which of the following?
o: An Android vulnerability that allows malware to pose as genuine applications
A Windows SMB exploit leaked by the Shadow Brokers
A worm targeting Siemens industrial controllers
A ransomware programme that encrypts master boot records
29.x: StrandHogg is an Android vulnerability that allows malware to impersonate genuine applications and steal user data. It was found by the Norwegian firm Promon in 2019.
29.tq: Use the operating system and impersonation behaviour to identify the vulnerability.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: Mirai is correctly matched with which of the following?
o: Botnet — hijacked Internet of Things devices used for massive DDoS attacks
Trojan — disguised software opening a backdoor
Adware — displaying advertisements through pirated software
29.x: Mirai is a botnet that hijacked IoT devices and used them to launch large-scale DDoS attacks.
29.tq: Match the named malware with its distinctive device class and attack method.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Appearance of Creeper on ARPANET
B. Appearance of Brain virus
C. Appearance of Stuxnet
D. Appearance of WannaCry
Which one of the following is the correct sequence?
29.x: Creeper appeared in 1971, Brain in 1986, Stuxnet in 2010 and WannaCry in 2017. Therefore, the sequence is A, B, C, D.
29.tq: Place the earliest and latest events first, then order the middle events by year.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. In 2016, a breach involving 3.2 million debit cards was reported.
2. Zomato suffered a data theft incident in 2017.
3. NotPetya notably affected Ukraine in 2017.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: All three statements are correct: the 2016 breach involved 3.2 million debit cards, Zomato faced data theft in 2017, and NotPetya affected Ukraine in 2017.
29.tq: Check each dated incident independently before selecting the coded combination.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: Which of the following was flagged by CERT-In in 2014 as a Trojan or related cyber-security threat?
29.x: CERT-In flagged Hikti, Dyreza Trojan and Shellshock in 2014. The other options are associated with different malware histories.
29.tq: Identify the correct item from a specific agency-and-year association.
29.sec: Named malware and attacks → type + origin (Creeper, Brain, Elk Cloner, WannaCry, Petya, EternalBlue, Stuxnet, Pegasus, StrandHogg), FIRST virus

29.s: Which cyber threat exploits a previously unknown and unpatched software flaw, thereby giving developers no prior opportunity to prepare a patch?
29.x: A zero-day exploit targets an unknown, unpatched vulnerability; developers have had effectively zero days to fix it.
29.tq: Use the exact technical definition rather than matching a general attack category.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, SQL injection, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s: The SolarWinds incident of 2020 is commonly cited as an example of which of the following?
29.x: In a supply-chain attack, a trusted vendor or supplier is compromised to reach the ultimate target; SolarWinds is a cited example from 2020.
29.tq: Identify the attack from its named real-world example.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s: Which one of the following best describes social engineering in cyber security?
o: Flooding a server with requests from a botnet
Encrypting traffic through a public network
Manipulating people through trust, urgency or curiosity to obtain an intended action
Injecting malicious database commands through a website input field
29.x: Social engineering targets human behaviour rather than merely exploiting a technical system. Trust, urgency and curiosity are commonly manipulated, and such methods can also be AI-enabled.
29.tq: Distinguish a human-targeting method from system-based attacks.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cyber espionage is often state-sponsored.
2. Spear-phishing and zero-day exploits may be used in cyber espionage.
3. Cyber espionage necessarily involves flooding a server with traffic.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: Cyber espionage is often state-sponsored and may employ spear-phishing and zero-days. Server flooding describes a denial-of-service attack, not a necessary feature of espionage.
29.tq: Find the one overbroad statement that confuses espionage with denial of service.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s:
With reference to denial-of-service attacks, consider the following statements:
1. A DoS attack seeks to deny genuine users access to a service.
2. A DDoS attack generally uses multiple machines, often organised as a botnet.
3. Mirai is an example of a botnet associated with DDoS attacks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: All three statements are correct. DoS/DDoS attacks overwhelm a system, while DDoS traffic originates from multiple machines such as a Mirai-linked botnet.
29.tq: Combine the general definition with the distinguishing feature and example.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s: Which of the following correctly differentiates spam from e-mail bombing?
o: Spam uses only voice calls, whereas e-mail bombing uses duplicate SIM cards.
Spam exploits unknown flaws, whereas e-mail bombing compromises a trusted vendor.
Spam is unsolicited bulk messaging, whereas e-mail bombing floods an inbox with huge volumes of mail to crash it.
Spam intercepts communication, whereas e-mail bombing alters database commands.
29.x: Spam consists of unsolicited bulk messages. E-mail bombing is the deliberate flooding of an inbox with very large volumes of mail, potentially crashing it.
29.tq: Separate two closely related terms by their specific purpose and effect.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s: An attacker secretly intercepts and alters communication between two parties without either party knowing it. This is called:
29.x: A man-in-the-middle attack involves secretly intercepting, and potentially altering, communication between two communicating parties.
29.tq: Match the defining action with the exact attack name.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s: SQL injection is primarily associated with which of the following activities?
o: Using a decoy system to study attackers
Routing traffic through an encrypted public-network tunnel
Forging a caller ID to impersonate another person
Entering malicious database code through a website input field
29.x: SQL injection places malicious database code into an application's input field in order to manipulate or access the underlying database.
29.tq: Link the attack to the technical entry point through which it operates.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s: DRDO-led Exercise Cyber Suraksha is associated with which of the following?
o: Developing a national antivirus for private companies
Training bank customers in digital payments over 12 months
Testing satellite navigation systems for civilian transport
Training the armed forces in cyber preparedness over 12 days
29.x: Exercise Cyber Suraksha is a DRDO-led 12-day exercise intended to train the armed forces in cyber security and preparedness.
29.tq: Use the organiser, duration and target group together to identify the exercise.
29.sec: Cyber threats → description matching (phishing, spam, e-mail bombing, spoofing, MITM, DoS/DDoS, zero-day, social engineering)  [APPSC]

29.s: Which of the following most accurately describes ‘digital arrest’ in the context of cyber crime?
o: A cyber criminal’s use of fake police or agency officials on a video call to frighten a victim and extort money
A court-ordered arrest carried out entirely through an online warrant
Police surveillance of cyber criminals through digital devices
Temporary suspension of a person’s digital identity by an internet service provider
29.x: Digital arrest is a criminal intimidation technique in which impostors claim that the victim is under arrest and demand money, often while keeping the victim on a video call.
29.tq: Reject the official-sounding but incorrect meaning and identify the criminal modus operandi.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s: The number of digital-arrest complaints recorded on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal declined from 1,23,672 in 2024 to which figure in 2025?
29.x: Digital-arrest complaints declined from 1,23,672 in 2024 to 58,249 in 2025.
29.tq: Read the year-wise figures carefully and avoid confusing the later year-to-date number.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s: Digital-arrest complaints recorded on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal stood at what number up to 30 June 2026?
29.x: The reported figure for digital-arrest complaints up to 30 June 2026 was 16,377.
29.tq: Distinguish a year-to-date figure from full-year complaint totals.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s:
The Supreme Court directions concerning digital-arrest cases included which of the following?
1. Framing standard operating procedures by the Centre, States, RBI and telecom authorities.
2. Use of zero FIRs.
3. Restoration of victims’ money.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: The directions covered SOPs by the specified authorities, the use of zero FIRs and restoration of money to victims.
29.tq: Treat each stated component of an institutional direction as a separate proposition.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s: Which one of the following correctly describes cyber slavery?
o: Trafficking people and forcing them to conduct cyber fraud, often in scam centres
Using a VPN to conceal a victim’s browsing history
Stealing a person’s identity to obtain a duplicate SIM
Selling stolen data only through encrypted e-mail
29.x: Cyber slavery involves trafficking victims and coercing them to operate cyber-fraud schemes, frequently from scam centres.
29.tq: Identify the crime from its coercion-and-trafficking element.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s:
Consider the following statements regarding cyber slavery and scam centres:
1. Telangana Police registered one of India’s first cases involving human trafficking to force victims to commit cyber fraud.
2. Scam centres connected with this phenomenon have been linked to Myanmar and Laos.
3. FIU-India flagged Rs 800 crore in cross-border laundering linked to the issue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: All three statements are correct: the Telangana case involved trafficking for cyber fraud, scam centres were linked to Myanmar and Laos, and FIU-India flagged Rs 800 crore in cross-border laundering.
29.tq: Check the institution, locations and quantified financial detail separately.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s: Which of the following is a characteristic of the dark web?
o: It is a secure government-only network used exclusively for defence communication.
It is a hidden part of the internet, reachable through tools such as Tor, and may host illicit marketplaces and data dumps.
It is the publicly indexed portion of the internet accessible through ordinary search engines.
It is a type of antivirus database maintained by CERT-In.
29.x: The dark web is a hidden part of the internet commonly accessed through tools such as Tor. It may contain illicit marketplaces, hacking tools and data dumps.
29.tq: Separate a hidden network from the ordinary publicly indexed web.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s: Identity theft and sextortion are correctly distinguished by which of the following statements?
o: Identity theft uses stolen personal data for impersonation, whereas sextortion involves blackmail using intimate images or material.
Identity theft means flooding an inbox, whereas sextortion means forging a caller ID.
Identity theft is committed only on the dark web, whereas sextortion is committed only through e-mail.
Identity theft always involves ransomware, whereas sextortion always involves DDoS traffic.
29.x: Identity theft involves using stolen personal information to impersonate a person. Sextortion involves blackmail or extortion using intimate images or similar material.
29.tq: Discriminate between two crimes by their distinct modus operandi.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s: Which of the following statutory provisions is associated with identity theft under the Information Technology Act?
29.x: Section 66C of the Information Technology Act is associated with identity theft. Sections 66E and 67A are relevant to offences involving privacy violations and sexually explicit material respectively.
29.tq: Use the offence-to-section association while avoiding neighbouring provisions.
29.sec: Cyber crime types - identity theft, sextortion, digital arrest, cyber slavery, dark web  [APPSC]

29.s: Which security mechanism is primarily intended to prevent unauthorised network access?
29.x: A firewall controls network traffic and helps prevent illegal or unauthorised access to a network or system.
29.tq: Match the security tool with its principal protective function.
29.sec: Security tools - firewall, antivirus, VPN, 2FA, passwords, honeypot, indigenous software → developer  [APPSC]

29.s:
Consider the following statements about common cyber-security tools:
1. Antivirus software helps prevent and heal infections.
2. A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel over a public network.
3. Two-factor authentication requires two independent proofs of identity.
4. A honeypot is a decoy system designed to lure and study attackers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: All four statements are correct. Antivirus addresses malicious infections, VPNs protect traffic through an encrypted tunnel, 2FA uses independent proofs, and honeypots attract attackers for observation.
29.tq: Verify each tool against its precise function before selecting the complete combination.
29.sec: Security tools - firewall, antivirus, VPN, 2FA, passwords, honeypot, indigenous software → developer  [APPSC]

29.s: A user authenticates an online account with a password and then an OTP or biometric proof. This arrangement is known as:
29.x: Two-factor or multi-factor authentication uses two independent forms of proof, such as a password combined with an OTP or biometric.
29.tq: Identify the security concept from the number and independence of authentication proofs.
29.sec: Security tools - firewall, antivirus, VPN, 2FA, passwords, honeypot, indigenous software → developer  [APPSC]

29.s: A security team intentionally exposes a decoy computer so that intruders can be attracted and their methods observed. The decoy is called a:
29.x: A honeypot is a decoy system designed to lure attackers and enable security teams to study their behaviour and techniques.
29.tq: Infer the tool from its deliberate decoy-and-observation role.
29.sec: Security tools - firewall, antivirus, VPN, 2FA, passwords, honeypot, indigenous software → developer  [APPSC]

29.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. BOSS Linux — C-DAC
2. Maya OS with Chakravyuh endpoint protection — Ministry of Defence
3. M-Kavach — C-DAC Hyderabad
4. CERT-In — CVE Numbering Authority for products made in India
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
29.x: All four pairs are correctly matched: BOSS Linux is associated with C-DAC, Maya OS with Chakravyuh with the Ministry of Defence, M-Kavach with C-DAC Hyderabad, and CERT-In with CVE numbering for products made in India.
29.tq: Start with the sure developer pair and verify each institutional association.
29.sec: Security tools - firewall, antivirus, VPN, 2FA, passwords, honeypot, indigenous software → developer  [APPSC]

29.s: Maya OS, associated with Chakravyuh endpoint protection, was developed by which organisation?
o: DRDO exclusively for Exercise Cyber Suraksha

29.s: In the process of encryption and decryption, which one of the following is correct?
o: Plaintext is converted into ciphertext during encryption and converted back during decryption using a key
Plaintext and ciphertext are identical forms of information
Ciphertext is converted into plaintext during encryption

3. Key sharing is one of its principal challenges.

29.tq: Combine the operating principle, example and limitation of one technical system.

29.s: Which of the following is the characteristic feature of asymmetric cryptography?
o: It is confined to hashing operations
It uses no key during encryption
It uses a public-private key pair and forms the basis of PKI
It uses a single password for every user
29.x: Asymmetric cryptography uses a mathematically related public key and private key pair and underlies Public Key Infrastructure (PKI).
29.tq: Identify the defining feature and application of a confusable technical pair.
29.sec: Cryptography terms - encryption, decryption, symmetric vs asymmetric, digital signature, hashing

29.s:
With reference to a digital signature, consider the following statements:

2. The signature is verified using the sender's public key.
3. It helps establish origin and integrity of the message.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: A digital signature is generated with the sender's private key and verified with the corresponding public key; it helps prove the message's origin and integrity.

29.sec: Cryptography terms - encryption, decryption, symmetric vs asymmetric, digital signature, hashing

29.s: Which one of the following correctly describes hashing?

A process that uses only a sender's private key to sign documents
A method of sharing the same secret key with all users
A one-way process producing a fixed-length digest, in which any change alters the hash
29.x: Hashing is one-way and produces a fixed-length digest. Even a small change in the input changes the resulting hash; SHA-256 is an example.
29.tq: Separate hashing from encryption and digital signatures by its defining properties.
29.sec: Cryptography terms - encryption, decryption, symmetric vs asymmetric, digital signature, hashing
